shoal_e16_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Five, the carrier office posted departures already completed during the fire week. Yue read one line twice because a tool seller had hoped the office would move it into the future. The boat had sailed on its actual date. The seller's stock had not been received aboard it. A later departure could be booked as new work, but the lost buyer meeting belonged to the week that had already passed.

shoal_e16_open_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_02.text: The seller wanted someone to say the missed meeting had not mattered. His buyer had arranged other stock and declined a fresh order. That answer was within the buyer's ordinary rights and left the seller with a real commercial loss. Han Pei received the actual evidence under its permitted scope. He did not call the refusal cruelty merely because the seller was already tired of hearing that other people had limits.

shoal_e16_open_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_03.text: Near the door, an apprentice waited with a sealed message to an inland master. Her trial date had passed while road seats were diverted to defined emergency work. The master had accepted another applicant after the deadline. She could write again, but she no longer held the original place. Yue asked what ordinary receiving help she wanted now. The apprentice wanted the failed journey acknowledged on her actual record, not a story saying fate had meant something better.

shoal_e16_open_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_04.text: Han entered the completed facts and supplied the permitted copy. The apprentice paid the ordinary message charge from her own money after checking its current price. She then asked about another master whose notice remained open. That was a different offer, with a different deadline and less pay. Hope for it did not erase the first refusal. She took the notice home to decide whether the new work would suit her.

shoal_e16_open_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_05.text: The port's freight-signal station had also missed two inspection dates. Qualified staffing and materials had gone to the actual fire response, and those appointments were not quietly performed by an empty room. The association would need new accepted dates. Lin could not stand at the seawall and become a station until its crews returned. Its temporary ordinary warning posts remained staffed only for the hours their employers had actually funded.

shoal_e16_open_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_06.text: Sui Yan walked the current boundary with the watch captain and closed one ordinary access lane where damaged masonry still awaited qualified assessment. People objected because the detour took longer. They were right about the inconvenience. The captain could explain the present hazard and actual next review without claiming that the inconvenience was imaginary or that a cultivation stage could clear the lane by walking through it first.

shoal_e16_open_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_07.text: Yue took the detour to her receiving shift and arrived at the appointed time because she had left earlier. A fisherman behind her had not seen the notice and missed a current sale. He cursed the closed lane, then asked where future notices would be posted. Sui's clerk added a second permitted display at the road he used. Better notice would help later journeys; it could not sell the fish already returned unsold to his basket.

shoal_e16_open_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_08.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Six, the fifth completed receiving week paid twenty-five copper for its actual five shifts. One final weekly settlement remained after the last accepted work. Yue counted her present money and paid current room and meals under the existing rate. She had learned to separate being scheduled to earn from having earned. The distinction became especially plain while helping people whose expected trade had vanished between one carrier notice and the next.

shoal_e16_open_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_09.text: A supplier's clerk asked whether the receiving room would remain open indefinitely. The new two-hundred-forty-copper appointment ended on Day Three Hundred Fifty-Five, with final settlement the next day. Any further work needed its own scope, people, and money. Han could identify requests worth proposing. He could not make Yue's current paid hours continue by leaving her name on a list after its accepted term had finished.

shoal_e16_open_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_10.text: The clerk brought two pending tasks that could fit one spare unassigned interval on Day Three Hundred Forty-Eight. A current school packet needed a checked ordinary dispatch receipt before its new route closed. A harbor worker wanted help receiving a sealed family message through a permitted contact chain. Both used ordinary clerical skills. The current office staff had accepted other hours, and neither task would be hidden inside their already full appointments.

shoal_e16_open_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_11.text: The school packet contained actual permitted teaching sheets, not the irreplaceable originals lost or retained in earlier salvage. Its sender had arranged this new copy under its own source rights and budget. Missing the present road would postpone this edition, not prove that a future road had been traveled. The family message concerned a private relative whose address needed current confirmation. Its content would remain sealed unless its owner chose otherwise.

shoal_e16_open_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_12.text: Yue asked the senders what the offered help would change. The school's departure clerk could receive the packet only during the present interval. The worker's contact person could verify the address only at that same hour before leaving town. Neither wanted Yue to promise the entire journey. They wanted her to perform one actual receiving task that made the next ordinary step possible. She could choose one or leave both to later arrangements.

shoal_e16_open_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_13.text: The worker was an ordinary woman named Nao, who swept the western market under a separate employer. Her brother had moved after a previous landlord raised the rent. She did not want his private circumstances made into public testimony. She had heard he was unwell through a cousin but possessed no clinical facts. The message asked what help he actually wanted and whether he would accept a visit. Worry had not granted her authority to plan it for him.

shoal_e16_open_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_14.text: The school sender knew her new packet could wait. She also knew another missed school road would leave teachers using an older permitted edition through the next term's first weeks. It was not a medical emergency. It was a real educational opportunity that a helpful person could lose by treating every unurgent hour as infinitely replaceable. Yue read the ordinary receipt list and asked where the accepted copying payment had come from.

shoal_e16_open_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_15.text: The copying source belonged to the current school's separate small print allocation. It did not depend on Yue's surviving earlier salvage or on the post-fire care deposit. The sender showed the current permitted extract and kept her private household money out of the conversation. Nao showed the accepted message contact's present window. These were concrete enough offers that Yue could say yes to one without making the unchosen person's concern disappear.

shoal_e16_open_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_open_16.text: Yue's last unassigned interval before the final receiving week would be long enough for one task and a return walk. Her elbow's ordinary baseline had been checked, while the old overhead shoulder limit remained. She needed neither new qi input nor medical authority to receive a packet. She also had her own reasons to rest and could decline. She chose to spend the offered finite hours where she thought she could be useful.

shoal_e16_dispatch_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_dispatch_choice.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Eight, one spare interval overlapped two current receiving windows. The school needed its newly funded permitted packet received onto this road before the deadline. Nao needed a sealed family message's address confirmed by a contact leaving town. Yue could perform one ordinary clerical task. The other would need a later arrangement, while every previously missed departure remained missed.

choices.text: Receive the school's new packet onto its current carrier.
Help Nao confirm and receive her sealed family message.

shoal_e16_school_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_01.text: Yue met the school sender at the actual ordinary dispatch table. The permitted packet was tied in a plain cover with its current edition and intended receiving school written outside. She checked the sheets the sender offered for that purpose, not every private note in the sender's bag. A page intended for an older class had been included by mistake. The sender replaced it before asking the carrier to receive the final packet.

shoal_e16_school_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_02.text: The correction cost several ordinary minutes. Yue asked the clerk whether the current deadline still allowed proper receiving rather than rushing him to sign unread terms. It did. He inspected the outside cover and named the actual carrier custody that would begin today. The receiving school would need its own later acknowledgment. A stamp here could not prove the packet had already reached a distant room full of children.

shoal_e16_school_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_03.text: A current copy of the carrier's ordinary receipt went to the school sender. The accepted packet entered the carrier's proper custody before departure closed. The sender thanked Yue for catching the misplaced page. It would have embarrassed a teacher and confused a class, but neither claimed it would have destroyed the entire school. The useful consequence had an ordinary scale and did not need a threatened catastrophe to deserve the hour spent preventing it.

shoal_e16_school_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_04.text: The boat's loading officer then stopped a different crate because its actual weight exceeded the submitted figure. The sender argued that the boat still floated. The officer held the present limit and demanded a corrected load plan. Yue watched from the permitted public side. Her own small task qualified no power to move the extra crate aboard. The crew's refusal, inconvenient and unspectacular, was part of what kept this departure within its accepted capacity.

shoal_e16_school_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_05.text: At Nao's contact window, no additional suitable helper attended. Nao came herself but could not complete the address verification before the contact's ordinary departure because the required receiving counterpart was absent. The contact gave a possible later route through a cousin and made clear it was not yet accepted. Her sealed message remained with her. Concern for her brother had not become a performed journey simply because the school packet now had a receipt.

shoal_e16_school_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_06.text: Yue met Nao afterward at the market's edge. Nao said she understood the choice and was still unhappy about the missed window. Yue accepted both sentences. She did not tell her that children mattered more or that a family could always wait. Nao wanted to return to work before her employer's next ordinary interval. Yue left her the current public contact hours where a later arrangement might actually be examined.

shoal_e16_school_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_07.text: The school sender invited Yue to watch a short lesson using the edition that remained locally available. It was an ordinary invitation after paid school hours, with no obligation to endorse every line. The teacher asked children to compare an illustrated road with the road they knew. A child pointed out a water trough absent from the picture. Another pointed out that the picture showed a bridge before its actual repair had been completed.

shoal_e16_school_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_08.text: The teacher let them mark the discrepancies in a permitted class copy instead of defending the printed road as more real than their observations. Yue recognized the exercise's purpose without pretending it licensed a public copy of someone else's private appendix. These were current teaching pages with their own source terms. The children's corrections would be checked locally before any new edition was offered. A useful question could precede a reliable answer.

shoal_e16_school_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_09.text: After the lesson, one child asked whether the packet's boat had sailed yet. Yue described the actual receiving she had witnessed and the posted departure, then said arrival still needed its own acknowledgment. The child seemed disappointed that a receipt contained so little adventure. His friend said a boat full of paper might get wet. The teacher asked them what the cover was meant to do and which failures it could not prevent.

shoal_e16_school_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_10.text: The later school acknowledgment arrived through its own actual message route. The packet had reached the named receiving school with the permitted contents intact. Its teachers would decide how to use it within the accepted edition's scope. Yue did not travel with that message or gain a second fee. She had chosen a current dispatch hour, and the fulfilled educational road now existed beside Nao's still-unfulfilled earlier family contact.

shoal_e16_school_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_11.text: Nao's later receiving inquiry remained open at the ordinary contact office. Her brother's actual wishes had not arrived. She could seek a new route, decline one too costly, or ask another suitable helper. The harbor had not abandoned her, but Yue's choice had failed to preserve a particular opportunity she had wanted. A future useful arrangement would be new work. It would not make this missed contact window disappear from her week.

shoal_e16_school_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_school_12.text: Yue returned the school's copied receipt after its proper acknowledgment had been recorded. The sender retained its source record; Yue kept only her own ordinary note of the offered hours. She could remember the class without owning it. On the walk back, she saw Nao sweeping sand from the market entrance and did not interrupt her paid work to ask for reassurance. Respect sometimes meant leaving a disappointed person enough room to be disappointed.

shoal_e16_family_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_01.text: Yue met Nao outside the contact office at the actual offered hour. Nao carried the sealed message and a separate ordinary address sheet she permitted Yue to read. The contact knew the brother's current neighborhood but had not accepted permission to reveal his household circumstances. Yue asked what could actually be confirmed. Nao wanted a usable receiving address and an offered message route, not a stranger's private clinical account.

shoal_e16_family_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_02.text: The contact checked the ordinary address with the receiving counterpart before its departure window closed. The brother had agreed to receive family messages there. That was a narrow permission and did not prove he wanted every visitor Nao might bring. Nao corrected the cover, paid the current accepted message charge from her own money, and handed the sealed message to the proper carrier under its actual custody receipt.

shoal_e16_family_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_03.text: Yue witnessed the receiving without opening the message. The carrier named its next ordinary stage and the expected acknowledgment process. Nao asked how soon a reply might return. He gave the current route estimate and explained that the brother would decide whether and when to answer. She disliked the uncertainty. It was nevertheless better than an address known to be wrong and a comforting promise no carrier could keep.

shoal_e16_family_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_04.text: At the school table, the present packet deadline passed without the extra receiving interval fulfilled. The sender kept the actual permitted sheets and asked about a later departure. That new road remained available for consideration, not already booked. The intended school would begin the term using its older permitted edition. The current educational opportunity was lost even though no patient had been denied care and no dangerous shipment had been forced onto a boat.

shoal_e16_family_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_05.text: The school sender told Yue the result in an ordinary brief message. Yue did not answer that family worry was more important. The sender had done real copying work and hoped it would be used sooner. Yue acknowledged the missed window and returned the unused receiving directions. They could consider a later offer without pretending she had spent the same hour at both offices. An honest refusal could leave someone properly disappointed.

shoal_e16_family_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_06.text: Nao went back to her market shift after the message had entered its accepted custody. She had not bought a journey herself or received a promise to cure her brother. The swept entrance remained her employer's ordinary task. Yue passed the market later and saw her bargaining over a broom replacement. Concern had not suspended all the other questions by which she lived. She could worry about a relative and still insist on better bristles.

shoal_e16_family_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_07.text: Several days later, a reply reached the actual offered receiving address. Nao chose to tell Yue only that her brother had answered and wanted no visit yet. He welcomed messages and had his own people nearby. She was relieved to hear from him and hurt by the refusal. Both responses belonged to her. Neither made his choice invalid or gave Yue permission to interpret a sealed family reply for the town.

shoal_e16_family_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_08.text: Nao asked whether sending another message would seem foolish. Yue said the reply's actual offered terms should matter more than her own guess. If he had welcomed messages, Nao could decide what she wanted to send within that invitation. It would need its own ordinary cost and route. The fulfilled first contact had made a real relationship exchange possible. It had not assigned Yue the role of directing it afterward.

shoal_e16_family_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_09.text: The school sender arranged a new later dispatch under its own accepted road budget. It was not the missed original window, and the first weeks using the older edition remained past. Yue heard about the new arrangement at the public board, where the sender had chosen to post it. The packet did not punish her by vanishing forever. Its delayed educational consequence remained a real cost of the earlier choice.

shoal_e16_family_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_10.text: The teacher adapted her first lessons to the older pages actually present. She asked children to compare their local road with its illustration and identify changed features. The absence of the new edition did not make her helpless or transform her into a cultivator's dependent. It gave her extra ordinary work. A useful adaptation could coexist with wishing the intended packet had arrived on the earlier road.

shoal_e16_family_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_11.text: Nao invited Yue to a brief cup of tea after the market closed. She repeated no private sentences from the reply. She talked about her brother's childhood habit of hiding sweet rolls behind a water jar and about a broom that ought to be ashamed of its workmanship. Yue laughed. The family contact had opened a modest private acquaintance, while the school dispatch she had declined remained somebody else's useful work.

shoal_e16_family_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_family_12.text: Yue left when the offered visit ended. Nao had another message to consider and no demand that Yue carry it. The school sender had its new road and no demand that she call the delay harmless. She could remember both consequences without making either person into a measure of her moral worth. The harbor's ordinary relationships continued with useful moments, refusals, and a week that could not be spent twice.

shoal_e16_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_01.text: The carrier office kept an ordinary wall calendar showing completed departures in darker ink than future ones. Some visitors wanted only the future rows. Others came to see a date that would never carry their name. The clerk could help them ask about a new road, but he would not move a dark line forward because looking at it hurt. Yue understood why that refusal could sound cold to someone who had waited too long for a kindness.

shoal_e16_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_02.text: A widow brought a letter written before her husband's last ordinary coastal trip. The fire had delayed a copy she wanted sent to his sister. Her husband had died months earlier from an illness unrelated to the sheds, and the town's new disaster had made people stop asking about the old one. She wanted the sister to receive the letter, not to have her loss included in a public fire account.

shoal_e16_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_03.text: Han identified the ordinary copying service and its current fee, leaving the private original with her until she accepted the actual work. The widow could afford the copy and wanted to inspect it before dispatch. Yue received the offered order under her paid scope. She neither invented a grant for it nor treated the woman's grief as proof she should surrender the letter to a public archive.

shoal_e16_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_04.text: The copied letter contained a complaint about a poorly made stool and a promise to bring home citrus if the price was sensible. It was not a heroic final speech. The widow said that was why she wanted his sister to have it. She remembered him most clearly when he was cross about furniture. Yue checked the copy against the original under the woman's actual permission and returned both for her acceptance.

shoal_e16_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_05.text: One line had been missed near the fold. Yue stopped the receiving and showed the exact omission. The copyist corrected it before the widow approved the work. Nobody congratulated Yue as though she had saved the dead man. She had caught a copying error in an ordinary paid room. The widow was grateful for the useful care and then asked whether the dispatch office would still be open after she ate lunch.

shoal_e16_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_06.text: The actual new departure received the approved copy on its own date. The sister's later receipt would belong to another receiving. The widow took the original home. Her husband had not returned, and the lost earlier dispatch remained lost. A new useful act could be worth doing without rewriting the years before it. Yue washed the ordinary copy weight after the shift because someone's lunch had left oil on its underside.

shoal_e16_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_07.text: On Day Three Hundred Forty-Nine, the last scheduled receiving week began. Yue worked the first of its five actual four-hour shifts, with the final settlement still due after completion. The remaining owner requests had specific people and sources. Two qualified readers would finish their accepted tasks under the same finite appropriation. New requests beyond its capacity would be recorded for a later proposal, not silently inserted as unpaid obligations.

shoal_e16_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_08.text: One owner wanted a drawing declared fully recovered because enough of its shape remained to sell a promising story. A qualified reader refused that description. The actual surviving portion could support limited work, and the missing annotations still mattered. The owner could choose whether to commission another test from an appropriate source. He could not use Yue's receiving signature as a certificate that she had read absent ink.

shoal_e16_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_09.text: Another owner wanted every doubtful tool destroyed so no later mistake could embarrass her. The receiving room offered the actual findings and disposal choices within her rights. She chose to retain some items marked out of current service for separate ordinary assessment. Her caution was understandable; her first impulse was not the only possible safe answer. The room's task was to receive her actual authorized decision, not admire the most dramatic one.

shoal_e16_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_10.text: At midday, a sailor argued that Lin's six pairs ought to carry a warning across the whole harbor. Yue named the quarter-unit local marker task she had actually qualified and its source ceiling. It could not power a sea wall or replace staffed warning posts. The sailor said ordinary posts were slow. She agreed that staffing and routes needed improvement. Her body was not a hidden unlimited source that unwilling officials had failed to ask for.

shoal_e16_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_11.text: Yan Su arrived before the argument grew into a contest of imagined strength. He wanted the sailor at an actual rope inspection later that afternoon if the man accepted its ordinary paid scope. The sailor knew ropes and accepted. The quarter-unit task remained small. A person disappointed by that limit could still contribute useful skills elsewhere without being humiliated into submission by a cultivator's demonstration.

shoal_e16_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_12.text: That afternoon a heavy cloud covered the shoal without becoming a catastrophe. Ordinary boats took their current weather precautions and some work paused. Rain fell long enough to change the lane's smell. It did not need to expose a secret enemy or test every promise the town had made. Yue ate under an awning and watched a child try to keep one paper hat dry with both hands.

shoal_e16_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_13.text: The hat dissolved at its fold. The child cried with a seriousness that made nearby adults lower their voices. His father offered to help make another when they reached home, not to restore the first one by declaring it had been worthless. Yue kept her dry working pages under their proper cover and let the child's small loss belong to him. Rain had room for both ordinary disappointment and practical care.

shoal_e16_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_14.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty, Bo completed his fifth four-copper rehabilitation session. Twenty copper of the thirty-two session line had now been spent on actual visits. The practitioner checked the current leg and permitted a limited progression under ordinary supervision. Bo found the new movement awkward and wanted to compare himself with the faster recovering worker. The practitioner returned to his actual observation and the next-day signs they needed to watch.

shoal_e16_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_15.text: Jin asked whether the house could rearrange a stool and table to reduce Bo's repeated twisting. The practitioner addressed the suitable ordinary change within the offered scope. They measured their own room afterward. No public housing choice had been made on their behalf. Their present room remained imperfect, but they could alter one daily difficulty without renting a future promised space they had not accepted or paid for.

shoal_e16_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_16.text: Bo later told Yue that he had spent an entire morning thinking about a small screw, not his leg. He seemed surprised by the pleasure. The screw belonged to an actual customer's requested estimate, and he had not yet accepted the repair itself. He could do a narrower part of his old work while still losing much of its former income. Yue asked about the screw because that was the subject he wanted to discuss.

shoal_e16_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_17.text: At the next receiving shift, the qualified reader brought a report with a clearly separated ordinary uncertainty. Han wanted the summary brief enough for a busy owner to read. The reader wanted the limitation impossible to overlook. They revised the wording together instead of dropping it to make the page handsome. Yue copied the accepted version only after both named what their own role could approve.

shoal_e16_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_18.text: The owner read the report twice and commissioned no immediate work. The cost of a proper further test exceeded what she could currently spend. Keeping a tool out of use was a real business consequence, not a failure of imagination. She chose to store it under the advised ordinary conditions and examine a later offer. Nobody awarded Yue another cultivation capacity because the owner had made a prudent refusal.

shoal_e16_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_19.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-One, the fifth five-copper restricted-income payment reached Bo. Twenty-five of thirty had actually been paid, with the final installment future on its scheduled date. He and Jin used their own household account to decide current meals and work materials. They did not treat the approaching end as an insult from the provider. They did argue about what would happen after it, because a finite useful payment left real needs behind.

shoal_e16_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_20.text: Han received a new supplier petition asking for public money to replace every anticipated sale. The petition gave actual past losses beside speculative future profits. He asked the supplier to distinguish them. The supplier considered that a hostile question. He Ming said workers had also been asked to distinguish performed hours from hoped-for hours. The supplier returned the next day with a narrower actual loss statement that could be examined.

shoal_e16_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_21.text: Rong Sui did not sign the supplier's broad petition. He had his own damaged delivery costs and preferred a claim he could defend. Another factor accused him of betraying their group. Rong answered that a group could be harmed by a number it could not explain. The quarrel did not make him benevolent or dishonest by itself. He remained a businessman who wanted payment and knew unsupported figures could defeat a genuine request.

shoal_e16_rejoin_22.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_22.text: Yue listened from her ordinary receiving table and did not adjudicate their motives. Her accepted task was to keep the submitted sources and consents clear for the people who would actually decide. It mattered whether a public statement named a worker who had agreed to appear there. It mattered whether a restricted note had been copied beyond its scope. The upcoming account discussion would need the actual source path, not a tidier substitute.

shoal_e16_rejoin_23.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_23.text: Song Mei sent a public performance notice for the following week under her own current venue agreement. Yue hoped to attend after her paid term closed. The notice did not promise a private meal, and its ticket price remained ordinary money. Song's independent artistic work had continued through the harbor's other troubles. Her next road interests were not a post automatically opened by the Six-Reach association.

shoal_e16_rejoin_24.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_24.text: The innkeeper asked whether Yue wanted to reserve her current bed beyond the receiving term. She could pay one period at the ordinary rate and decline a longer promise. She agreed only to dates she could fund from present own money. He put those dates in his book, leaving the later line blank. The blank felt less frightening than a bargain that assumed she would remain useful in town forever.

shoal_e16_rejoin_25.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_25.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Two, Yue worked the fourth shift of the final week. A customer arrived near closing and requested a full new appraisal outside her ordinary receiving role. She took the current request for its proper next process and explained the actual hours. The customer was angry. She could remain civil without pretending that his anger created qualified time, a reader, and a source of payment before the room closed.

shoal_e16_rejoin_26.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_26.text: Afterward she walked with He Ming to the public market. He wanted to buy a small gift for the departing older household's eventual visit, not send it on an imaginary road that nobody had booked. They examined dried fruit and a cloth cover. He chose the fruit because the household had named it in an ordinary conversation. A gift could remember a person without requiring a published story about how well they had adapted inland.

shoal_e16_rejoin_27.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_27.text: He Ming asked whether Yue would leave soon. She said her present term was ending and no outgoing role had been accepted. He nodded and did not turn the answer into a loyalty test. A town could value a worker and still let her next work belong to another place. He would miss hearing her question a bad summary before breakfast. She would miss his habit of answering with a better question.

shoal_e16_rejoin_28.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_28.text: Near the market, the apprentice with the missed trial date posted a notice offering current ordinary repairs within her actual skills. She had decided against the lower-paid distant offer. That was neither triumph nor collapse. She wanted income while considering another road. A customer brought a torn bag, and she quoted the price before taking it. Yue saw the transaction and hoped the stitching would go well without declaring the earlier lost apprenticeship necessary.

shoal_e16_rejoin_29.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_29.text: The widow whose letter had been copied returned to ask about its current acknowledgment. None had arrived yet. Han checked the actual message record and told her what was known. She was disappointed, then asked whether the office still sold the small envelopes she liked. It did. She bought two for future letters she might choose to write. Waiting could include ordinary purchases and impatience without becoming a test of virtue.

shoal_e16_rejoin_30.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_30.text: On Day Three Hundred Fifty-Three, Yue completed the final four-hour shift, making thirty actual shifts under the new receiving appointment. The two qualified readers also finished their accepted source work. Closure and final payment remained on their proper dates. She put the completed requests in their actual custody places and left pending work clearly identified. An ending hour could be useful because everyone knew which promises had actually been performed.

shoal_e16_rejoin_31.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_31.text: She did not take the owners' drawings away as a private collection. Those sources retained their respective rights and receiving records. Her own practice notebook, local observations, and permitted ordinary copies remained hers under their actual scopes. The supplier appendix returned to Lark custody long ago did not reappear in her pack because another job had ended. She closed the cupboard she was authorized to close and handed its key to the named clerk.

shoal_e16_rejoin_32.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_32.text: The public room would remain staffed for its ordinary existing functions after this finite appointment. Its new special receiving hours would end unless another source accepted them. People would feel the difference. Han posted the actual future timetable before taking down the special one. He wanted a visitor to know where a request might go rather than arrive to a room whose old sign made a promise nobody now held.

shoal_e16_rejoin_33.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_33.text: Yue stood outside for a moment after her last shift. The harbor sounded much as it had on the first day, but she could now distinguish the packing bell from the carrier bell and knew which ordinary lane became crowded after supper. Familiarity was a useful change. It had not returned an original lost mould, restored a failed apprenticeship, or taught her to lift fire away from a sea.

shoal_e16_rejoin_34.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_34.text: She walked past the school wall where the corrected alarm diagram still hung under its weather cover. Beside it, children had pinned new pictures of boats and a beetle keeper. One boat was impossibly tall. Nobody presented it as a loading plan. Yue liked that the public wall could hold checked instructions and openly imagined things in separate ordinary uses. The town would need both as it decided which work to fund next.

shoal_e16_rejoin_35.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_rejoin_35.text: At home she opened her notebook to the pending account meeting. Some sources had been offered publicly, some under restricted appointments, and some did not exist beyond a person's memory. Those distinctions would shape what the workers could actually challenge. She would attend in her named receiving role if asked, then leave that role when its actual hours ended. Tonight she put the notebook down and ate before the food went cold.

shoal_e16_close_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_01.text: The innkeeper's daughter asked whether closing a job meant Yue could now sleep late. Yue said some mornings might permit it. The girl considered that a disappointing reward for so much work. She preferred a whole day of sleeping if a job was finished. Her father said the girl still owed him one turn carrying clean linen upstairs. Yue let their disagreement proceed without volunteering to erase it.

shoal_e16_close_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_02.text: From the landing she heard a courier explaining why a packet had returned unopened. The named receiver had declined it under its offered terms. The sender was angry and wanted the refusal called a failure of delivery. The courier had actually reached the person and received an answer. He could show that completed work while respecting the receiver's choice. A road did not guarantee the reply its sender desired.

shoal_e16_close_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_03.text: Yue wrote that distinction beside her own current departure questions. She wanted a role that would let her do something toward the mine, yet she had not decided which scope she could sustain. An association invitation might carry property, people, or survey work. Each would require terms. She left room for a refusal rather than treating the road on a map as a contract she had already accepted.

shoal_e16_close_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_04.text: Later the school tower keeper rang the night hour. His actual repair had been performed, and the rough sound Yue remembered had diminished. She would not have noticed it on her first week in town. Knowing continuities made departure harder to imagine. It also made her glad that people whose work she could barely describe had kept a clock running while everyone argued about grander signs of recovery.

shoal_e16_close_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_05.text: She checked the flowers in the uneven cup. One stem had browned, and she removed it before changing the water. The rest would last a little longer. She had bought them for her own room, not as a promise that broken things always became beautiful. Outside, the lane grew quiet enough to hear a neighbor turning a page. Yue went to bed while the quiet was available.

shoal_e16_close_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e16_close_06.text: Morning would bring closure work for the named clerk and questions for the people preparing the account meeting. Yue's performed shifts were complete, with the final settlement still future. The workers would need their own sources and courage. She could help within an offered role, but she could not give them every missing number or remove every cost of speaking. She woke ready to hear what they wanted to attempt.
